title: Contamination Recognition, Isolation and Corrective Action

content.overview: Contamination is both a culture-loss problem and a diagnostic signal about the propagation system. Visible fungal or bacterial growth requires containment, but repeated contamination patterns also require source tracing and workflow correction.

vocabulary.definition: Microbial contamination that is present but not yet visibly expressed in culture.
Physical or procedural separation of suspect material from clean production cultures.
A documented change intended to remove the cause of a detected process failure.

sections.title: Visible contamination is not the only risk
sections.body: Some contaminants appear rapidly while others emerge after subculture or acclimatization. Clean-looking material should not be assumed pathogen-free without an appropriate testing strategy.

sections.title: Isolation prevents one failure becoming a batch failure
sections.body: Suspect vessels should be separated and handled after clean cultures. Opening contaminated vessels in the transfer workflow can spread propagules through tools, surfaces or airflow.

sections.title: Patterns reveal process weaknesses
sections.body: Contamination clustered by donor, operator, date or medium lot can identify likely sources. Corrective action should follow the evidence pattern rather than changing many variables simultaneously.

workedExamples: Repeated bacterial contamination from one donor line points to source-material or internal contamination risk rather than random vessel failure.
Contamination appearing across several unrelated genotypes after one transfer day suggests reviewing that day's workspace and handling process.
commonMistakes: Opening contaminated vessels beside clean cultures.
Treating all contamination as random bad luck.
Changing medium, disinfectant and workflow simultaneously so the cause cannot be identified.
content.practicalApplication: For each contamination event, record organism appearance, vessel ID, donor, operator, transfer date, medium lot and neighboring batches. Review clusters before choosing corrective actions.
content.summary: Contamination control combines isolation, disposal, traceability and root-cause analysis. The goal is not only to remove failed vessels but to prevent recurrence.
